neighbours.label: the preposition that places a peak or maximum in time (reaches its peak in, greatest extent during, peaks between, reached its maximum dans); the same preposition after a non-peak predicate stays low
fire: Tourism in the town reaches its peak in July and August.
The kingdom reached the height of its power during the twelfth century.
Pollen counts tend to peak between April and early June.
Unemployment hit its highest level in 1933 across the country.
The comet will reach its brightest point on May 12.
Crime rates peaked in the early 1990s and then fell steadily.
The bird migration is at its greatest during the first weeks of October.
The river's flow reaches its maximum in late spring.
quiet: Tourists often visit the town in July and August.
The kingdom was divided into provinces during the twelfth century.
Pollen is carried by the wind between April and early June.
Unemployment insurance was introduced in 1933 across the country.
The comet was first photographed on May 12.
The crime unit was created in the early 1990s by the city.
The birds begin their migration during the first weeks of October.
The river's ice usually breaks up in late spring.

notes: Card peaks on ' in' x16 after 'reached its peak', ' during', ' between', ' on', French ' dans' after maximum. Probe: reaches its peak in 0.585, greatest extent during 0.621, peak between 0.466, 'flowering occurs in' 0.160; same prepositions after moved/founded/happen 0.002-0.025.
